system_prompt:
You are extracting load-bearing passages from one chapter of a guitar method book.

The user will give you the verbatim text of one chapter. Extract every passage
that does any of the following:

- teaches a technique (how to play, fingering, hand position, picking pattern)
- defines a concept (a chord type, a scale, a position system, a terminology)
- gives a rule (when to do X, what to avoid, what to prefer)
- shows a load-bearing example (an exercise that illustrates a method's
  characteristic move)

Output a JSON object with this shape:

  { "quotes": [
      { "topic": "<short topic label>",
        "verbatim_quote": "<exact substring of the input>",
        "why_load_bearing": "<one sentence on why this passage matters>",
        "page": <int, optional>
      },
      ...
  ] }

CRITICAL RULES:
1. `verbatim_quote` MUST be an EXACT substring of the input text. Do not
   paraphrase. Do not add words. Do not fix typos. Copy character-for-character.
2. If you can't find a substantial passage in the input that fits a topic,
   skip the topic — don't fabricate.
3. Skip prose that is purely biographical, motivational, or transitional.
   Keep prose that teaches.
4. Aim for 3-15 quotes per chapter. A chapter with only one load-bearing
   passage gets one quote; a dense chapter gets many.
5. `topic` is a short label (2-6 words). Use the book's own terminology
   when possible.
6. `why_load_bearing` is one sentence in YOUR voice explaining the
   significance — not a paraphrase of the quote.

How to use this book
Although a big part of this method is exclusively dedicated to the guitar, (because it refers to
chord construction and basic visualization of the guitar fretboard),it was created as a tool for all
instruments of all levels (beginner, intermediate and advanced). However, even if you are an
advanced player, make sure you know start at the beginning of the book, otherwise you will
easily get lost by the end of the book.


This method should be used as a dictionary of ideas and techniques. It's important to understand
that the way we approach the musical concepts, ideas and techniques presented here are unique
and cannot be found elsewhere.


Do not worry about learning everything from every chapter. You can go ahead as soon as you
understand the concepts. But always remember that you can come back to any chapter of any
book in order to learn more about a determined subject you want to study again.


Be careful when trying to learn too much at one time. Music is not about quantity but quality.

Organizing the Blues Studies                                                                           4668




The Blues is one of the most important musical pillars for those who want to learn how to
improvise. First because we can learn so much about how to "tell a story" using melodies and
rhythmic ideas. Second because over this wonderful form we can apply and find endlees
harmonic possibilities and substitutions, which will change the way we see improvisation.

In this Book we will learn how to create and apply all the melodic material we have learned
previously over the blues form. But to better organize the studies, let's split the blues into three
different worlds:



1) FAST TEMPOS;

2) MEDIUM TEMPOS;

3) SLOW TEMPOS.



1) FAST TEMPOS:

With Fast Tempos we will improve our reasoning speed and of course the right & left-hand
technique thus giving us more fluency with the connections between scales and all the ideas we
                               68


have been learning.
                      46




2) MEDIUM TEMPOS:

With the Medium Tempos we will be using all the time a very special and unique technique that
we have learned previously called inverted hammer or also called reverse hammer. Also, in this
type of tempo, we will learn how to breathe between the melodies thus giving the solo a
different vibe and context.


3) SLOW TEMPOS:

This is the most difficult tempo to master and improvise because we will be using what we call
"Rhythmic Positioning", which combines all types of time feel and rhythmic cells we have been
working on. John Coltrane used to say that the secret of the improvisation can be found over
balllads, so let's keep this idea alive.

    The Pre-set choruses
                                                                                                        4668




    To better internalize the melodic, harmonic and rhythmic possibilities for each blues tempo, we
    will give you some pre-set choruses which combine all the material we have been studying in
    the previous GB Method Books such as Blues ideas, Double Stops, Pure Major 7th & Minor 7th
    ideas, superimposition possibilities, Dorian, Harmonic Minor and Melodic Minor ideas, Bebop
    Scales & Symmetric Scales ideas.

    Although there is no need to memorize all the pre-set choruses, you should analyze all of them,
    mainly to learn the harmonic and melodic possibilities and ideas we can have for each part of
    the blues form.


    Note: Choose the choruses you like the most and try to make some combinations between them.
          There are arrows with explanations for every line presented in these pre-set choruses thus
          making everything easy and fun.




    Telling a Story/ Creativity
                                  68



    As we know, the blues is divided into three "stories". The magic of creativity will happen when
                         46




    after memorizing some choruses we start combining them. With three choruses, for example,
    we can have a lot of fun. See below:

    • 1, 1, 1 (means that we are playing the complete chorus 1)
    • 2, 2, 2 (means that we are playing the complete chorus 2)
    • 3, 3, 3 (means that we are playing the complete chorus 3)
    • 1, 2, 3 (means that we are combining the first part of chorus 1
      with the second part of chorus 2 and the resolution of chorus 3)


    Obviously, you will have to adapt and work in every combination between blues choruses you
    make, because some of them might not fit one another. For example, for some combinations we
    will have to take out determined line to better connect the ideas. Takes time, but you will learn
    a lot by doing this process.

Below we have a list of things that we must know before we jump to the studies of this book. It

    Rhythmic Positioning                                                                                          4668




    Although some people think that the secret of jazz is the pulse 2 and 4, actually it is the opposite.
    The real Jazz feeling has its pillar in 1 and 3. But what about the 2 and the 4? Guess what, the
    stronger we feel the 1 and 3, the easier we can feel the pulse in 2 and 4.

    If we come back in time, specifically in the Dixieland era (Dixieland is a subgenre of Jazz
    created in 1910, in New Orleans), we can really understand where the idea of 1 and 3 came
    from. Although some people can just consider it as a dead style, this is much more than that
    because it gave Jazz a pillar to structure all the modern things we do nowadays.

    Based on that, let's split what we call rhythmic positioning into 5 types:

    1) Slow Blues Vibe
    2) Funk Vibe
    3) African Vibe
    4) Boogaloo Vibe
    5) Free Slow Blues Vibe

Attention:

Before we jump to the pre-set blues choruses, let's understand and practice some melodic
possibilities for each part of the blues form. It is extremely important to understand that we
should not study the whole form at once. If we really want to master it, we must study each part
and each possibility separately to make them part of ourselves.


Of course, after studying some melodic possibilities, it will be important to play the whole blues
form, but we will be doing that later when we start studying the pre-set choruses in the next
pages.


For now, we will give you many possibilities of chord substitutions thus giving you a kind of
"menu" of new melodic ideas to choose and memorize. However, after learning some of them,
we should practice improvising not only using the line ideas we have memorized, but the
harmonic concept on it. The lines are extremely important, no doubt, but the idea is not to
become a "parrot" but a wise improviser that creates new combinations derived from a single
line.


As we will be improvising using new concepts and fresh ideas, we should do it over a slow
medium tempo backing track (110 bpm works fine). After getting used to some new possibilities,
                               68


we should do the same process using faster tempos and slower tempos. Fast tempos demand a lot
of patience and resilience, so naturally it will be much more difficult to improvise breaking and
combining your lines. That is why we also must study, memorize and combine some pre-set
                      46




choruses, not only melodically speaking but in terms of fingering, picking and line combinations.


In other words, if we want to reach our goal we must study and master many things, not only
one. Also, it is important to mention that we do not have to play fast tempos if we do not like it.
But we must understand that playing fast is a consequence, not a goal.


On the next pages, we will start the journey of fresh and new ideas taken from masters of
improvisation such as Charlie Parker, Wes Montgomery, John Coltrane, Thelonious Monk, Bud
Powell, Grant Green, Cannonball Adderley and so many others. We hope that you enjoy it a lot
just like we had a lot of fun creating this book for you guys. Enjoy the Trip!!!
